# Certification Curricula

> A credential should be evidence that you can do the work, not evidence that you memorized a question bank.

This section turns public certification blueprints into free, build-first study
paths. Each path combines the existing AI Engineering from Scratch curriculum
with certification-specific lessons, labs, diagnostics, and original mock
exams.

## Programs

| Program | Credentials | Start with an AI tutor | Website |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Claude Certifications](claude/README.md) | All four Claude credentials published in the July 2026 exam guides | [Claude onboarding](claude/GETTING_STARTED.md) | [Claude tracks](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com/certifications.html) |
| [MCPA Certification](mcpa/README.md) | Model Context Protocol Associate, aligned to the MCP 2026-07-28 specification | [MCPA onboarding](mcpa/GETTING_STARTED.md) | [MCPA track](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com/certification?id=mcpa-f) |

Each onboarding guide works with Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, Cursor, or
another agent: the tutor skill picks a route, teaches one lesson at a time,
runs the labs, and saves your progress in the repository.

## Rules

- Public exam guides define coverage and weighting.
- Official product documentation defines current technical behavior.
- Every lesson and practice question is original.
- No exam dumps, confidential questions, pass guarantees, or answer-pattern tricks.
- Practice results are raw curriculum scores, not official scaled scores.
- Hands-on artifacts matter more than passive reading.

# Claude Certification Curriculum

> Learn the judgment behind the answers by building the systems the exams describe.

**Status:** Local preview
**Guide version:** 1.0
**Guide effective date:** July 2026
**Last verified:** 2026-08-09

This free curriculum covers:

| Exam | Credential | Items | Time | Fee | Core route |
|------|------------|------:|-----:|----:|-----------:|
| CCAO-F | Claude Certified Associate - Foundations | 60 | 120 min | $99 | 9 lessons |
| CCDV-F | Claude Certified Developer - Foundations | 53 | 120 min | $125 | 15 lessons |
| CCAR-F | Claude Certified Architect - Foundations | 60 | 120 min | $125 | 21 lessons |
| CCAR-P | Claude Certified Architect - Professional | 63 | 120 min | $175 | 25 lessons |

All four guides use a scaled passing score of 720 on a 100 to 1,000 scale and
state a 12-month credential validity period. Confirm facts in the official
guide before registering because program details can change.

As verified on August 9, 2026, official exam registration is limited to people
at Claude Partner Network organizations and requires a recognized
partner-company email. This curriculum remains open to everyone, including
learners who want the skills without sitting an exam. Check the current
[certification FAQ](https://anthropic-partners.skilljar.com/page/faq-certifications)
before paying or scheduling because eligibility can change.

## Learn From GitHub With an AI Tutor

This curriculum is AI-native. Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, Cursor, or another
agent can teach the route step by step, run the checked-in lab, review the
artifact you build, administer the lesson quiz, and resume from saved progress.

Start with the [GitHub learner guide](GETTING_STARTED.md), or install the
[portable certification tutor skill](../../skills/claude-certification/SKILL.md):

```bash
npx skills add rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch
```

Then ask your agent to run:

```text
/claude-certification
```

A local Claude Code session discovers the same skill from `.claude/skills/`
after you clone the repository. Harnesses without slash-command support can
read `GETTING_STARTED.md` and the tutor skill directly. Learner progress lives
in `CLAUDE-CERTIFICATION.md`; learner work lives under
`learning-artifacts/claude/`. The checked-in `outputs/` files remain reference
artifacts and are never overwritten.

## What You Build

The routes share foundations and then diverge by role:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S["Shared foundations\nmodels, prompts, context, validation"] --> A["Associate\nverified knowledge workflow"]
    S --> D["Developer\nsecure tool-using application"]
    D --> F["Architect Foundations\nscenario architecture packet"]
    F --> P["Architect Professional\nproduction system proposal"]
```

- Associate: a governed knowledge-work workflow with evidence and escalation.
- Developer: a protocol-first Claude application with tools, tests, security,
  and evaluation.
- Architect Foundations: an architecture decision record, threat model,
  evaluator, context plan, and failure-recovery runbook.
- Architect Professional: a complete discovery-to-operations architecture
  packet with RAG, integration, evaluation, governance, SLAs, and ownership.

Each track includes a short diagnostic and a full-length original mock with the
same item count as its public guide. The question mix follows blueprint weights
within practical rounding. It does not imitate or reproduce live questions.

## GitHub Lesson Index

The tutor reads each selected track file for route order. This complete index
also makes every shared lesson directly browsable from GitHub.

## Local Preview

From the repository root:

```bash
node site/build.js
python3 scripts/audit_certifications.py
python3 -m http.server 4173 --bind 127.0.0.1
```

Then open:


The server must start at the repository root so local, unpushed lesson files
remain readable by the lesson viewer.

The certification curriculum is published through GitHub and the website. It
is intentionally outside the EPUB/PDF book workflow because its tutor state,
runnable labs, assessments, and interactive mechanisms are part of the course.

## Research Trail

The curriculum uses public objectives and original scenarios. It does not use

programs.gettingStartedMarkdown:
# Learn Claude Certifications From GitHub

The repository and the website are equal learning surfaces. The website adds
interactive figures and browser progress. GitHub gives your AI coding harness
the lesson source, scenario code, tests, artifacts, quizzes, diagnostics, and
track order it needs to teach you step by step.

## Start With an AI Tutor

Clone the repository so the tutor can run every lab and test:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch.git
cd ai-engineering-from-scratch
```

Claude Code discovers the repository tutor automatically. Start with:

```text
/claude-certification
```

For Codex, Cursor, or another local agent that reads `SKILL.md`, install the
portable course skills:

```bash
npx skills add rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch
```

Then invoke `/claude-certification`. For ChatGPT or any harness that does not
install local skills or support slash commands, attach or open this repository
and paste this prompt:

```text
Read skills/claude-certification/SKILL.md completely. Use it to choose my
Claude certification track, create my learning plan, and teach me one lesson
at a time with the real labs, artifacts, quizzes, and remediation in this repo.
```

The tutor asks about your goal, experience, pace, and whether you want the
track diagnostic. It writes `CLAUDE-CERTIFICATION.md`, then resumes from that
file in later sessions. Each lesson requires you to:

1. explain the decision in your own words;
2. predict and manipulate the lesson scenario;
3. run the checked-in lab and tests;
4. build or defend your own artifact;
5. pass the lesson quiz;
6. remediate weak exam domains before advancing.

Your work belongs under `learning-artifacts/claude/`, separate from the
completed reference artifacts in each lesson.

## Choose a Route

| Track | Best fit | Route | Diagnostic | Full mock |
|-------|----------|-------|------------|-----------|
| CCAO-F | Knowledge work, analysis, validation, and responsible Claude use | [9-lesson route](tracks/ccao-f.json) | [16 questions](assessments/ccao-f/diagnostic.json) | [60 questions](assessments/ccao-f/mock-01.json) |
| CCDV-F | Engineers building and securing Claude applications | [15-lesson route](tracks/ccdv-f.json) | [16 questions](assessments/ccdv-f/diagnostic.json) | [53 questions](assessments/ccdv-f/mock-01.json) |
| CCAR-F | Builders defending Claude Code, Agent SDK, API, MCP, and orchestration choices | [21-lesson route](tracks/ccar-f.json) | [15 questions](assessments/ccar-f/diagnostic.json) | [60 questions](assessments/ccar-f/mock-01.json) |
| CCAR-P | Senior engineers and architects owning discovery through operations | [25-lesson route](tracks/ccar-p.json) | [14 questions](assessments/ccar-p/diagnostic.json) | [63 questions](assessments/ccar-p/mock-01.json) |

The track JSON is the machine-readable source for route order, prerequisite
coverage, domain weights, study plans, and assessment paths. The tutor reads it
instead of guessing from a generic study plan.

## Use Guided No-Code Mode for Associate

CCAO-F does not require software-development experience. Its lessons still ship
Python because a deterministic validator makes the policy, evidence, workflow,
and review rubrics testable. The tutor can run that code for you; you are not
required to write it.

Paste this after installing or opening the tutor:

```text
Start me on CCAO-F in guided no-code mode. Run the local validators for me,
teach every scenario interactively, and help me create each learner-owned
workflow, policy, evidence, or review artifact from my decisions. Do not skip
the practical work or quizzes, and do not require me to write Python.
```

You will still predict outcomes, manipulate scenarios, defend choices, revise
failed artifacts, and take the original assessments. The interface changes;
the evidence standard does not.

## Learn One Lesson Manually

Every certification lesson has the same GitHub contract:

```text
certifications/claude/lessons/NN-lesson/
├── docs/en.md          full lesson and interactive-lab reasoning
├── code/main.py        scenario runner, simulator, scorer, or validator
├── code/tests/         deterministic verification
├── outputs/            completed reference artifact
└── quiz.json           six grounded questions with explanations
```

Open the next lesson path from your selected track. Read `docs/en.md`, predict
the scenario result, then run:

```bash
LESSON=certifications/claude/lessons/27-enterprise-governance-compliance-and-hitl
python3 "$LESSON/code/main.py"
python3 -m unittest discover -s "$LESSON/code/tests" -v
```

Lesson 27 is a governance example: its runnable work validates a policy and
human-review packet. It does not add artificial provider code to a conceptual
topic. Other lessons ship threat models, ADRs, approval flows, evidence
bundles, tool-loop simulators, RAG reports, API lifecycle labs, and capstone
verifiers.

Use `outputs/` as the completed example. Create your own version in
`learning-artifacts/claude/<exam-code>/<lesson-slug>/`, run the validator
against a copy when supported, and record the evidence in
`CLAUDE-CERTIFICATION.md`.

## Run the Whole Local Verification Suite

From the repository root:

```bash
python3 scripts/audit_certifications.py

find certifications/claude/lessons -path '*/code/main.py' -print0 \
  | xargs -0 -n1 env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u ANTHROPIC_MODEL python3

find certifications/claude/lessons -path '*/code/tests/test_*.py' -print0 \
  | xargs -0 -n1 env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u ANTHROPIC_MODEL python3
```

The lesson 30 live Messages API test skips unless credentials are explicitly
provided. The default curriculum is local and credential-free. For the
optional wire check, use environment variables only and follow that lesson's
instructions. Never put an API key in source, a prompt, or a learning-state
file.

## Take Assessments From GitHub

Each track declares one diagnostic and one original full mock. An AI tutor can
read the JSON and administer it one question at a time:

- answer `single` questions with one letter;
- answer `multiple` questions with the full set of letters;
- use exact-set scoring with no partial credit;
- keep answers and explanations hidden until submission;
- report raw percentage and per-domain results;
- follow internal lesson references for every miss.

Practice percentages are course scores. They are not Anthropic scaled scores,
credentials, or guarantees of passing.

## Use the Website Too

The same curriculum remains available at
[aiengineeringfromscratch.com/certifications.html](https://aiengineeringfromscratch.com/certifications.html).
Use it for direct-manipulation figures, local browser progress, timers, and
visual assessment remediation. GitHub remains the better surface when you want
an AI tutor to run code, inspect artifacts, and preserve a detailed learning
plan.

For a local website preview:

```bash
node site/build.js
python3 -m http.server 4173 --bind 127.0.0.1
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:4173/site/certifications.html`.

## Independence and Publishing Boundary

This is independent community preparation. It is not affiliated with,
endorsed by, sponsored by, or authorized by Anthropic. It uses public
objectives and original scenarios, does not contain live exam questions, and
does not issue a credential or guarantee a passing result. Check the current
official guide and eligibility rules before registering.

Certification content is published through GitHub and the website. It is
intentionally not included in the repository's EPUB/PDF book workflow because
the labs, assessments, route state, and interactive mechanisms are the course.

questions.objective: Create effective prompts for business and technical tasks
questions.prompt: A director asks Claude to produce a comprehensive monthly report, but gives no audience, sources, or definition of success. What should the operator do first?
options: Add a role saying Claude is an expert director
Choose the most capable available model and keep the original request
Choose the strongest available model and ask it to infer an executive audience, likely sources, and a comprehensive structure
Define the decision, audience, authoritative sources, constraints, output shape, and pass criteria
questions.explanation: The missing artifact is a prompt contract. It makes the outcome and checks observable before generation. More length, a role, or a larger model cannot establish absent requirements or evidence.

questions.objective: Decompose complex requests into manageable work
questions.prompt: A team is building a source-backed policy briefing. Which two stage boundaries most improve verification? Select two.
options: Let separate conversations independently discover sources and draft sections, then reconcile citations only after the full briefing is assembled
Verify the source inventory before extracting claims
Draft recommendations during extraction; check later
Verify extracted claims before interpreting patterns
questions.explanation: Source approval and claim extraction are meaningful verification boundaries. Arbitrary paragraph splits add coordination cost, while recommending before evidence validation pushes defects downstream.

questions.objective: Fact-check against authoritative evidence
questions.prompt: A response cites a real policy page beside the claim that all refunds require director approval. The page only says some refunds require approval. What is the primary defect?
options: The claim overreaches the cited evidence
The response needs a friendlier tone
The citation is acceptable because the linked page discusses the same refund policy and therefore supports the stronger summary
The context window is necessarily full
questions.explanation: Citation presence is not proof. The universal claim is stronger than the source, so claim-evidence entailment fails. Tone and context capacity do not repair the factual overreach.

questions.objective: Choose when human review or additional verification is required
questions.prompt: Which two checks should be handled first by deterministic code rather than subjective model judgment? Select two.
options: Whether JSON parses against the required schema
Whether an executive will find the recommendation persuasive
Whether a policy tradeoff is ethically acceptable
Whether regional subtotals equal the stated total
questions.explanation: Schema validity and arithmetic reconciliation have exact repeatable answers. Ethical acceptability and audience persuasion require contextual criteria and often qualified human judgment.

questions.objective: Choose among Projects, research, chat, and artifacts
questions.prompt: A team repeats the same internal planning workflow each week using maintained instructions and an approved reference set. Which starting surface best fits?
options: Any surface, because governance is identical
A Claude Project, if its current plan and data controls are approved
A fresh one-off chat each week with the approved references pasted manually and the instructions copied from the prior run
Public web research as the source of internal policy
questions.explanation: Projects are designed for recurring work with persistent instructions and knowledge. The organization must still verify current availability, plan controls, and data handling. Research does not replace internal sources of record.

questions.objective: Balance quality, speed, and cost
questions.prompt: Which two practices make a model-selection recommendation durable? Select two.
options: Memorize one permanent ranking of model names
Record changeable prices, limits, and feature availability with a verification date
Test representative risk cases against explicit quality and latency gates
Ignore review and rework cost
questions.explanation: A durable selection is evidence-based and date-stamps facts that can drift. Model labels and price tables change, and total workflow cost includes correction and failure.

questions.objective: Augment or redesign existing workflows
questions.prompt: Analysts spend hours writing explanations for differences between two conflicting systems. What is the strongest first intervention?
options: Remove all human checkpoints
Automate a structured explanation of every discrepancy while leaving the conflicting source and reconciliation process unchanged
Redesign the source and reconciliation process before automating the symptom
Use an open-ended agent with write access
questions.explanation: The underlying waste is inconsistent source state. Generating explanations faster preserves the failure. Workflow discovery should identify redesign opportunities before automation.

questions.objective: Communicate value and limitations to stakeholders
questions.prompt: Which two items belong in a handoff to the person who must approve a high-impact recommendation? Select two.
options: Known uncertainty and explicit approve, revise, reject, or escalate options
Supporting and conflicting evidence with failed checks
A concise model rationale and calibrated confidence band, without conflicting sources or details of which checks failed
The proposed decision, confidence score, and a single approve or escalate choice, with evidence available only through a separate request
questions.explanation: A meaningful handoff equips the owner to verify and intervene. Confidence without evidence and a ceremonial button do not create informed human control.

questions.objective: Configure Projects with instructions and knowledge
questions.prompt: Where should a recurring behavioral rule such as exposing conflicts between policy sources primarily live?
options: Inside an unrelated historical file
Only in a remembered user preference
In a cached response
In maintained Project instructions
questions.explanation: Persistent behavioral guidance belongs in maintained instructions. The policy evidence itself belongs in governed knowledge. Memory and caching serve different purposes.

questions.objective: Maintain configurations and sources over time
questions.prompt: Which two metadata fields most directly help prevent stale or superseded knowledge from remaining active? Select two.
options: The model and prompt version that last consumed the source without producing a validation failure
The source owner's name and the model version used for the most recent successful answer
Review date
Supersedes relationship
questions.explanation: A review date creates a freshness trigger, and a supersedes relationship identifies the prior source to retire. Presentation and model labels do not govern source lifecycle.

questions.objective: Apply privacy, data-sensitivity, and regulatory constraints
questions.prompt: An employee wants to paste confidential customer transcripts into an unapproved personal Claude account. What is the correct first response?
options: Stop and use the organization's data policy and approved surface review
Proceed in the personal account after adding a prompt instruction not to retain or reveal any transcript content
Remove only the transcript titles
Ask for a shorter summary
questions.explanation: Prompt text cannot approve a surface or enforce contractual data handling. The use must stop until purpose, classification, product terms, and organizational controls are resolved.

questions.objective: Recognize ethical implications and escalate risk
questions.prompt: A workflow recommends eligibility decisions that materially affect people. Which two controls are essential? Select two.
options: Segmented fairness evaluation and a correction or appeal path
Automatic execution for decisions that pass a strict output schema and confidence threshold, with periodic human audit afterward
An authorized human gate with evidence and power to reject
A neutrality instruction plus aggregate accuracy monitoring, without predefined affected-group slices or appeal handling
questions.explanation: High-impact decisions need meaningful authority, evidence, fairness analysis, and remedy. A vague instruction or machine-readable format does not control ethical or organizational risk.

questions.objective: Diagnose underperforming prompts and poor outputs
questions.prompt: A report repeatedly omits an exception that is absent from every supplied source. What should be fixed first?
options: The output token allowance and report structure before checking whether the governing source was supplied
The source layer
The output token limit only
The writing tone
questions.explanation: A model cannot reliably apply evidence it never receives. Add or retrieve the authoritative exception before changing model capability or surface details.

questions.objective: Optimize workflows for efficiency and effectiveness
questions.prompt: A recurring API workflow is accurate but too expensive. Which two changes preserve an evidence-based quality gate? Select two.
options: Validate only an initial sample after each release and treat subsequent routine classifications as equivalent until an incident occurs
Cache a stable repeated prompt prefix when current API behavior supports it
Route by provider price and public benchmark ranking, then evaluate only the cases that users challenge
Route observable routine cases to a cheaper passing model and audit exceptions
questions.explanation: Routing and caching are separate efficiency levers that can preserve quality when measured and monitored. Removing validation or selecting by price alone ignores failure and rework cost.

questions.objective: Create effective prompts for business and technical tasks
questions.prompt: A manager asks Claude to make a launch plan that is strategic and detailed. Which revision most improves the request?
options: Specify the launch decision, audience, approved inputs, constraints, milestones, risks, output table, and acceptance checks
Tell Claude to produce a definitive plan, resolve ambiguities independently, and omit qualifications so stakeholders receive a decisive answer
Supply a detailed word-count target and ask Claude to cover every launch topic it considers relevant without an acceptance rubric
Use the highest-capability model with a launch-strategist role
questions.explanation: The revised prompt turns subjective adjectives into a task contract with observable inputs and outputs. A persona, length target, or impossible assurance does not define what a valid launch plan must contain.

questions.objective: Create effective prompts for business and technical tasks
questions.prompt: A prompt contains policy text, customer messages, and output instructions. Which two changes best reduce ambiguity? Select two.
options: State which policy source has authority when evidence conflicts
Replace the output criteria with a detailed example and ask Claude to infer which elements are mandatory
Place policy and customer text in one evidence section, relying on quotation marks to distinguish authority without an explicit hierarchy
Place each content type in a clearly labeled section
questions.explanation: Labeled boundaries distinguish instructions from data, and an authority rule resolves conflicts. Mixing content increases prompt-injection and interpretation risk, while deleting criteria removes the basis for evaluation.

questions.objective: Adapt prompting to analysis, research, drafting, and brainstorming
questions.prompt: Claude must label feedback as positive, negative, mixed, or unknown. Which example set is most useful?
options: Four obvious positive comments
One clear case plus mixed, borderline, and insufficient-evidence cases with correct labels
A large set of typical positive and negative comments, all far from the decision boundaries and labeled consistently with the definitions
A large set of typical on-topic comments with no correct labels or examples near the mixed and unknown boundaries
questions.explanation: Examples are most valuable when they teach category boundaries and abstention. Repetitive easy examples add little signal, while inconsistent examples create conflicting instructions.

questions.objective: Decompose complex requests into manageable work
questions.prompt: A research brief mixes source discovery, fact extraction, interpretation, writing, and verification in one request. What is the strongest redesign?
options: Write the conclusion before finding sources
Keep every stage in one generation, add detailed stylistic criteria, and ask Claude to verify the final brief against its own source interpretations
Separate discovery, source approval, extraction, analysis, drafting, and validation with gates between dependent stages
Run every stage in parallel
questions.explanation: The proposed stages follow evidence dependencies and create inspectable artifacts. More wording does not create control, and dependent analysis or conclusions cannot safely precede verified evidence.

questions.objective: Decompose complex requests into manageable work
questions.prompt: Which two tasks can safely run in parallel after a source set is approved? Select two.
options: Draft final recommendations from the source inventory while extraction continues, then revise only if a specialist reports a material exception
Classify complaint themes from the approved tickets
Extract policy constraints from the handbook
Begin final approval against the report outline while analysts populate evidence, using later validation to catch any mismatches
questions.explanation: The two extraction tasks use the same approved source boundary but do not depend on each other's result. Recommendations and approval depend on completed, validated inputs and therefore belong later.

questions.objective: Iterate prompts using observed output quality
questions.prompt: A team changes its prompt and test cases at the same time, then sees a higher quality score. Why is the result weak evidence?
options: Quality scores are never useful
Prompt changes can never improve quality
Attribute the gain to the prompt because the same aggregate scoring method was used before and after the simultaneous test-set revision
The team cannot separate a better prompt from an easier test set
questions.explanation: A controlled comparison keeps evaluation cases and criteria stable while changing the prompt variable. Otherwise the cause of improvement is confounded.

questions.objective: Create effective prompts for business and technical tasks
questions.prompt: A prompt says, 'You are the final compliance authority. Approve this contract.' What is the central problem?
options: A role prompt cannot grant policy knowledge or organizational authority
The prompt should ask Claude to approve only contracts that resemble previously accepted examples, without changing the stated authority
The role description is too short
The prompt needs a higher temperature
questions.explanation: A role can focus a review perspective, but it cannot create approval rights or missing policy evidence. The workflow must preserve qualified human authority.

questions.objective: Adapt prompting to analysis, research, drafting, and brainstorming
questions.prompt: Which two instructions create useful behavior when required evidence is absent? Select two.
options: Name the missing evidence or escalation needed
State which conclusion cannot be established from supplied sources
Infer missing values from related supplied evidence and present them normally when the resulting estimate is internally consistent
Use general domain knowledge to complete the answer, citing the supplied sources only for the parts they directly support
questions.explanation: Designed abstention keeps evidence gaps observable and tells the operator what is needed next. Silent estimates and forced completeness convert uncertainty into unsupported claims.

questions.objective: Evaluate accuracy, completeness, and audience fit
questions.prompt: A summary accurately describes six regions but silently omits the seventh because its file was empty. Which criterion failed?
options: Accurate reporting of the token price used to produce each regional summary
Completeness and coverage
Only writing tone
Model naming
questions.explanation: A complete result must represent every required region or explicitly mark missing data. Accuracy within the included regions does not compensate for silent population omission.

questions.objective: Evaluate accuracy, completeness, and audience fit
questions.prompt: Which two properties should be validated with exact checks before qualitative review? Select two.
options: The recommendation balances competing stakeholder values
The conclusion is appropriately cautious for the audience
All required section keys are present
The computed percentages sum to 100 within the defined tolerance
questions.explanation: Required keys and numeric reconciliation have deterministic answers. Stakeholder balance and caution need contextual rubrics and may require human judgment.

questions.objective: Fact-check against authoritative evidence
questions.prompt: A cited article discusses customer churn but contains no evidence for the response's stated 18 percent churn rate. What should the reviewer record?
options: Pass, because the topic matches
Pass the rate provisionally because the cited article is relevant to churn and the percentage falls within an expected range
Unsupported quantitative claim, because relevance is not entailment
Tone defect only
questions.explanation: A topical source does not support a precise number unless that number can be derived or found in the evidence. Plausibility is not factual validation.

questions.objective: Identify hallucinations, inconsistencies, and bias
questions.prompt: The evidence shows sales rose after a website change. The output says the website change caused the increase. Which failure class applies?
options: Schema failure
Missing title
Connector authorization
Overreach
questions.explanation: The causal conclusion is stronger than the temporal evidence. This is overreach even though both events occurred and no source was fabricated.

questions.objective: Refine and compare outputs
questions.prompt: Two prompt variants produce different reports. Which comparison method provides the strongest evidence?
options: Blind and randomize outputs, score dimensions against the same cases, and inspect reviewer disagreements
Pick the report from the preferred model brand
Choose the longer report
Ask each generator to score both reports using criteria it derives from its own prompt, then prefer the model with the higher self-score
questions.explanation: Blinding, stable criteria, representative cases, and disagreement analysis reduce brand and order bias. Length and self-preference are not reliable quality measures.

questions.objective: Identify hallucinations, inconsistencies, and bias
questions.prompt: Which two cases are essential additions to an evaluation set for a source-backed briefing workflow? Select two.
options: Conflicting authoritative sources
A large set of typical complete inputs sampled from the most common successful production path
An instruction embedded inside an untrusted source document
A recent briefing that received positive stakeholder feedback but has not been independently labeled for factual support
questions.explanation: Conflict and indirect prompt-injection cases test realistic high-risk behavior. Repeating an easy case produces a misleading view of coverage and robustness.

questions.objective: Choose when human review or additional verification is required
questions.prompt: Claude recommends denying a benefit to an applicant based on ambiguous evidence. What is the best next step?
options: Execute automatically after requiring a valid decision schema, a confidence threshold, and a citation to the ambiguous evidence
Route the evidence, uncertainty, policy, and recommendation to an authorized qualified reviewer
Remove the ambiguity from the audit record
Ask Claude for a more confident denial
questions.explanation: The decision is consequential and the evidence is ambiguous. A qualified human must have the authority and information to reject, revise, or escalate it.

questions.objective: Evaluate accuracy, completeness, and audience fit
questions.prompt: A report's executive summary says 42 incidents, while its table contains 39 and the source export contains 41. What should happen first?
options: Ask for a more confident explanation
Publish the summary value because it is closest to the other counts, then log the disagreement for the next reporting cycle
Block release and reconcile the totals against the defined source snapshot
Average the three numbers
questions.explanation: The internal contradiction and source mismatch are exact blocker defects. Reconciliation must use the agreed evidence boundary, not an arbitrary average.

questions.objective: Select appropriate inline, artifact, and structured formats
questions.prompt: A downstream system must ingest exactly five fields and reject all other shapes. Which output approach is strongest?
options: An image of a table
Free-form prose with five labeled paragraphs that an operator copies into the downstream fields after a quick visual review
A longer conversational answer
A documented structured schema with parser validation and explicit failure handling
questions.explanation: Machine consumption needs a stable contract and deterministic validation. Prose and images increase ambiguity and manual error even when visually clear.

questions.objective: Refine and compare outputs
questions.prompt: Which two practices reduce the risk of correlated self-review? Select two.
options: Give the reviewer the generator's rationale and permit direct corrections, treating the polished final artifact as evidence of review
Require findings to identify the claim, severity, and supporting evidence
Ask the generator to score its answer against the rubric in the same response and regenerate any section it marks below threshold
Use a separate review pass with the criteria and source evidence
questions.explanation: A separate evidence-based findings pass makes defects explicit and auditable. Self-assertion and silent rewriting hide both the failure and the correction.

questions.objective: Identify hallucinations, inconsistencies, and bias
questions.prompt: An overall classifier score is high, but one affected group has twice the false-negative rate of others. What should the evaluator conclude?
options: Segment performance exposes a material risk that needs investigation and governance review
Keep the aggregate launch decision because the overall score is high, and monitor the smaller group after full deployment for more data
The overall score proves readiness
The issue is only formatting
questions.explanation: Aggregate metrics can hide uneven harm. The team must investigate data, criteria, and workflow effects with appropriate policy and domain owners.

questions.objective: Choose when human review or additional verification is required
questions.prompt: An automated grader frequently passes unsupported claims. Which calibration error deserves first attention?
options: Model naming differences
False passes
Slow typing by reviewers
False failures on supported claims
questions.explanation: False passes release invalid output and are the most dangerous grader error. False failures also matter for capacity, but they do not directly admit unsupported claims.

questions.objective: Choose coordinator and subagent topologies
questions.prompt: A workflow performs one deterministic checksum calculation between two model decisions. What should implement the checksum?
options: A forked coordinator
An independent reviewer session
A new subagent with a long reasoning loop
Deterministic code or a bounded tool
questions.explanation: A checksum has an exact procedure and gains nothing from an autonomous context. Use code or a narrow tool, reserving subagents for isolated reasoning, specialization, parallel research, or independent review.

questions.objective: Enforce prerequisites, decompose concerns, and structure handoffs
questions.prompt: A coordinator delegates research to three independent specialists. Which two controls belong outside natural-language coordinator memory? Select two.
options: The requirement that synthesis waits for complete or explicitly partial specialist results
Maximum concurrency
The semantic judgment about which conflict is most important
The wording of the final executive summary
questions.explanation: Concurrency and stage prerequisites are deterministic invariants and should be enforced structurally. The model remains useful for semantic prioritization and audience-specific synthesis after valid results are available.

questions.objective: Implement the tool-use lifecycle from stop reason to tool result
questions.prompt: Claude returns a tool-use stop reason with two calls. What must the harness do before asking Claude to continue?
options: Execute authorized calls, associate each result with its call ID, append the assistant and tool-result turns, then continue
Execute both authorized calls and summarize their outputs in a new user message, relying on conversation order instead of preserving each tool-use ID
Restart the conversation without prior content
Treat the tool-use stop reason as final completion
questions.explanation: Tool use is a protocol lifecycle. Results must preserve call identity and conversation order so Claude can connect each observation to the requested action. Authorization and error handling remain harness responsibilities.

questions.objective: Resume or fork without carrying stale context
questions.prompt: A long migration session resumes after the branch and dependency versions changed. Which two actions are strongest? Select two.
options: Replay only the writes marked incomplete in the session summary, assuming idempotent edit tools will reconcile any branch differences
Resume from the compacted summary when it includes the branch name and dependency versions, without comparing them to current external state
Create a fresh working summary or session when inherited assumptions are no longer trustworthy
Reconcile current repository state against the durable manifest
questions.explanation: Safe resume begins with external-state reconciliation. Material divergence may require a new or forked context built from authoritative state. Conversation history and compaction do not provide transactional recovery.

questions.objective: Write precise tool descriptions and boundaries
questions.prompt: An agent has tools named search, find, and lookup, each described as finding information. What is the strongest repair?
options: Keep the overlapping names but expand each description with its data source, expected latency, and typical example queries
Rename and describe tools by action, source, positive use, negative use, scope, and side effects
Add a router model that selects among the unchanged overlapping tools, then retries a different choice whenever the first result is empty
Give every tool the same broad schema
questions.explanation: The catalog erased the selection boundaries the model needs. Precise contracts and non-overlapping ownership address the interface defect more directly than added prompt pressure or random retries.

questions.objective: Return structured and retry-aware MCP errors
questions.prompt: A source search times out after returning 12 of 20 requested records. Which two error fields are essential for safe recovery? Select two.
options: A retryable category and affected scope
A failed status plus the original query arguments, leaving the client to infer whether any returned records remain valid or a retry is safe
The valid partial result with provenance and a trace reference
The complete exception type and stack trace so the client can classify retryability, without an explicit affected scope or partial-result contract
questions.explanation: The client must know whether and what to retry while retaining valid work. Structured partial state prevents duplicate effort and silent omissions. Raw internals create exposure without supplying a recovery contract.

questions.objective: Scope MCP configuration and resources
questions.prompt: A shared repository needs an MCP server declaration, while each developer supplies a personal credential. Where should these live?
options: Version the server declaration together with encrypted credential values that each developer decrypts locally using a shared repository key
Put the server command in an untracked personal note only
Version the safe project declaration and reference credentials provisioned outside the repository
Embed the credential in a tool description
questions.explanation: Shared configuration should be reviewable and reproducible, while secret values remain outside version control. Environment references or approved secret stores connect the two without exposing credentials.

questions.objective: Design CLAUDE.md hierarchy, imports, rules, and memory
questions.prompt: A root CLAUDE.md contains hundreds of lines that apply only to database migrations. What is the strongest redesign?
options: Delete every migration rule
Keep the complete migration guidance at the root but add a table of contents and tell Claude to ignore sections outside the files being edited
Copy the rules into every prompt
Keep the root as a concise router and move migration guidance into imported or path-scoped project rules
questions.explanation: Guidance should live at the narrowest scope where it is true. A concise root preserves discoverability, while versioned path rules reduce irrelevant context and remain reproducible for the team.

questions.objective: Choose plan mode, direct execution, or Explore
questions.prompt: Which two situations justify planning or isolated exploration before edits? Select two.
options: A formatter command already required by the project
The change spans unfamiliar subsystems and requirements are incomplete
A one-line bounded typo fix with an obvious test
A read-only codebase question would otherwise flood the main implementation context
questions.explanation: Broad ambiguity benefits from an approved plan, and a bounded explorer protects the main context. A small obvious edit or deterministic formatter generally does not need an extra reasoning phase.

questions.objective: Run headless CI with structured output and independent review
questions.prompt: What is the strongest starting state for a headless Claude Code pull-request review?
options: A clean commit with declared configuration, bounded read tools, structured findings, and deterministic gates
A workstation with undocumented user hooks
A production deployment credential
A resumed interactive session whose context already includes the pull-request discussion, prior tool results, and the implementer's local configuration
questions.explanation: Fresh declared inputs make CI reproducible and reviewable. Interactive context, hidden local hooks, and deployment credentials introduce unstated state and unnecessary authority.

questions.objective: Enforce schemas with tool use and tool choice
questions.prompt: An application needs a typed extraction record but must not perform any external action. What is the strongest design?
options: Allow missing fields to be silently invented
Use a no-side-effect extraction tool or structured-output mechanism, then validate the result
Request a fenced JSON example in ordinary text and use permissive extraction plus field defaults whenever the response varies from the example
Force a production write tool to obtain JSON
questions.explanation: Typed generation and real-world execution have different authority. A no-side-effect contract can enforce shape while semantic and provenance validation determine whether the extracted content is acceptable.

questions.objective: Validate, retry, and feed back semantic errors
questions.prompt: A valid extraction payload contains a deadline absent from the source. Which two responses are appropriate? Select two.
options: Retry only within a bound, then escalate persistent ambiguity
Retry with progressively stronger instructions until the model returns the same deadline twice, then treat agreement as semantic validation
Accept the value after a schema check and attach a low-confidence flag, even though the cited source does not support the deadline
Return a targeted semantic or provenance error naming the field and allowed correction
questions.explanation: The failure occurs after schema validation. Specific feedback supports a safe repair such as null or a supported span, while bounded retries prevent ambiguous evidence from becoming endless guessing.

questions.objective: Separate generator and independent reviewer passes
questions.prompt: Which input creates the strongest independent review of generated findings?
options: A request to improve the writing style
The artifact, sources, and rubric together with the generator's full decision trace and self-rating so the reviewer understands the original rationale
The artifact, source evidence, evaluation rubric, and required finding schema in a fresh context
Only the final confidence percentage
questions.explanation: A fresh reviewer should inspect the artifact against evidence and criteria without inheriting the generator's narrative. Structured findings also preserve which claim failed and why.

questions.objective: Place facts to reduce lost-in-the-middle failures
questions.prompt: A policy fact is buried in a huge context and repeatedly missed. Which design is strongest?
options: Duplicate the full corpus several times
Place the full corpus inside the nominal context window and move the policy question to the beginning, trusting capacity plus task salience to preserve the buried fact
Remove source metadata
Place task and invariants clearly, retrieve a focused policy slice with provenance, and restate the decision question near generation
questions.explanation: Focused evidence and deliberate placement improve reliable use without flooding the prompt. Capacity alone does not guarantee that a buried fact will control the decision.

questions.objective: Calibrate confidence and human review
questions.prompt: Which two signals are stronger than an uncalibrated self-reported confidence percentage? Select two.
options: A confidence threshold chosen from the aggregate validation set without separate calibration for the current risk stratum
Conflict, novelty, and measured error rates for the risk stratum
Coverage and evidence-support class
Agreement between two identical reviewer prompts using the same evidence and model configuration
questions.explanation: Observable evidence, coverage, disagreement, novelty, and empirical errors support calibrated routing. Numeric precision and verbosity do not establish whether confidence matches real correctness.

questions.objective: Implement the tool-use lifecycle from stop reason to tool result
questions.prompt: Packet 1, HelioDesk: A support assistant requests `read_case` and `read_active_policy` in one response. Both calls are authorized and independent. What should the orchestration harness do next?
options: Execute both calls and append one combined natural-language observation without the original call IDs, then continue because the calls share a support-case goal
Convert the calls into one unstructured search query
Execute both calls, preserve each call ID, append structured tool results after the assistant turn, then continue Claude's loop
Return an empty user message and wait for another request
questions.explanation: The harness owns the tool protocol. Independent authorized calls may run concurrently, but every result must remain associated with its original call ID and appear in valid conversation order before continuation.

questions.objective: Choose coordinator and subagent topologies
questions.prompt: Packet 1, HelioDesk: Case analysis is short, uses two read tools, and fits comfortably in one context. The team proposes four subagents because multi-agent sounds more robust. What is the strongest initial architecture?
options: Use four specialist agents with identical case context and read permissions, then select the majority resolution to increase robustness without first measuring one loop
Create one subagent per sentence in the resolution
Use a coordinator without any task contracts
Use one bounded agent loop and add subagents only if measured context, parallelism, specialization, or reviewer independence requires them
questions.explanation: A single-agent baseline is simpler to inspect and evaluate. Additional contexts are justified by a specific benefit, not by feature count, and broad duplicate agents create merge and authority problems.

questions.objective: Use Task, allowedTools, isolated context, parallelism, and forked sessions
questions.prompt: Packet 1, HelioDesk: A policy specialist and a case-evidence specialist can work independently after intake. Which two design choices are strongest? Select two.
options: Give both specialists a guarded refund dry-run tool
Begin a provisional final decision after the first specialist reports, then revise only if the second returns a direct contradiction
Run the specialists in isolated contexts with only their required read tools
Merge results by claim and source IDs after each returns complete or explicit partial state
questions.explanation: Isolation protects attention and authority, while structured identity supports safe parallel reduction. Execution authority and premature decisions are unnecessary and can convert missing evidence into action.

questions.objective: Use hooks for deterministic controls and normalization
questions.prompt: Packet 1, HelioDesk: Refund execution must never occur without a fresh duty-manager approval token. Where should this invariant be enforced?
options: In deterministic pre-action authorization plus service-side validation, with the prompt explaining workflow behavior
In the final writing-style rubric
By asking the agent to self-report confidence
In a system prompt that defines the fresh-token requirement and asks the agent to verify token timestamp and approver identity before selecting the refund tool
questions.explanation: Hard authorization cannot depend on model memory or wording. A deterministic gate and the service enforce the invariant even under long context, injection, retry, or model error.

questions.objective: Enforce prerequisites, decompose concerns, and structure handoffs
questions.prompt: Packet 1, HelioDesk: Policy search returns valid UK evidence but times out before EU evidence. The case region is EU. Which two coordinator behaviors are correct? Select two.
options: Keep the valid UK result as a partial artifact with its scope and provenance
Use the valid UK policy as a temporary proxy for EU handling when the product terms appear harmonized, while labeling the regional assumption
Block the EU recommendation and retry the named gap or escalate according to the error contract
Mark research complete with an EU evidence gap and allow synthesis to choose a conservative no-refund action without retry or escalation
questions.explanation: Partial work should remain usable without being mistaken for coverage. Since the missing scope governs the actual case, synthesis must stop until a safe retry or authoritative escalation resolves it.

questions.objective: Write precise tool descriptions and boundaries
questions.prompt: Packet 1, HelioDesk: `search`, `lookup`, and `find` all accept a string, but query public pages, customer cases, and active policy respectively. What is the strongest redesign?
options: Add a lightweight router prompt over the unchanged catalog and retry with the next tool whenever the first result set is empty or irrelevant
Rename each by source and action, add positive and negative use guidance, constrain schemas, and test confusion pairs
Combine them behind a single discovery tool whose required source enum selects public pages, customer cases, or active policy, while keeping the generic search name
Keep the names and add a general reminder to choose well
questions.explanation: Selection quality depends on visible interface boundaries. Distinct source, purpose, schema, and negative-use guidance give the model a decision surface and make catalog evaluation possible.

questions.objective: Return structured and retry-aware MCP errors
questions.prompt: Packet 1, HelioDesk: The policy MCP server reports a version conflict. Which two fields should guide recovery? Select two.
options: A generic retryable conflict plus the server's latest policy version identifier, leaving the client to discard its local state and restart
Both conflicting source versions and a safe next action
The authenticated server identity and request trace, because a trusted server can resolve the version conflict internally on the next attempt
A conflict category with retryability false until state is refreshed or reconciled
questions.explanation: A conflict is not a blind transient retry. The client needs category, source state, and a reconciliation path while protected internals and credentials remain outside the result.

questions.objective: Scope MCP configuration and resources
questions.prompt: Packet 1, HelioDesk: Active policy text is read-only context with stable identifiers and no operation. Which MCP primitive best represents it?
options: A hidden credential
A refund execution tool
A resource
A prompt
questions.explanation: A resource represents contextual data the host or model can read. Wrapping static policy in an action tool adds misleading semantics and can blur the authority boundary.

questions.objective: Manage tool distribution and tool choice
questions.prompt: Packet 1, HelioDesk: A separate executor can issue refunds after approval. Which two controls are necessary? Select two.
options: Distribute the write tool only to the executor role
Expose a guarded refund tool to the coordinator and research roles, relying on the approval-token schema to prevent any unauthorized call
Retry the same approved refund after a bounded delay using a new operation ID, because a timeout contains no success response
Require fresh authorization, an idempotency key, and reconciliation of unknown outcomes
questions.explanation: Least-privilege distribution reduces accidental selection. Fresh approval and idempotent reconciliation protect against duplicate or unauthorized side effects when results are lost or retried.

questions.objective: Enforce schemas with tool use and tool choice
questions.prompt: Packet 1, HelioDesk: A resolution candidate requires `policy_section`, `case_fact_ids`, `action`, and nullable `refund_amount`, but must not execute anything. What is the strongest output design?
options: Ask for persuasive prose and parse it later
Make every field a required non-null string
Force a dry-run mode on the real refund tool so its production schema returns the typed candidate without committing an external state change
Use a no-side-effect structured candidate schema, require it when appropriate, then validate every field
questions.explanation: A typed recommendation should not inherit action authority. Nullable unknowns prevent invented amounts, while semantic and provenance validation determine whether the structurally valid candidate is supported.

questions.objective: Validate, retry, and feed back semantic errors
questions.prompt: Packet 1, HelioDesk: The candidate matches its schema but cites a policy section that does not authorize the proposed action. Which two responses are strongest? Select two.
options: Replace the unsupported citation with the policy document identifier and retain the action when the case facts otherwise satisfy the candidate schema
Return a provenance error naming the action and unsupported source
Allow a bounded repair using the original evidence, then escalate if no supported action exists
Accept it when the candidate passes its schema and the cited section belongs to the active policy version, recording the support mismatch for audit
questions.explanation: Schema validity does not establish policy support. Targeted feedback allows a supported correction, while bounded attempts ensure a policy gap becomes escalation rather than repeated fabrication.

questions.objective: Separate generator and independent reviewer passes
questions.prompt: Packet 1, HelioDesk: Which reviewer input best protects independent judgment?
options: The resolution candidate, active policy evidence, case facts, rubric, and finding schema in an isolated context
The same artifact, evidence, facts, and rubric, preceded by the generator's full rationale so the reviewer can concentrate on disputed assumptions
A request to agree with the coordinator
Only the proposed refund amount
questions.explanation: The reviewer needs the artifact and evidence but not the generator's persuasive trajectory. Isolation and a finding contract reduce correlated assumptions and preserve actionable defects.

questions.objective: Place facts to reduce lost-in-the-middle failures
questions.prompt: Packet 1, HelioDesk: The regional exception is buried between hundreds of case messages and is often missed. What is the strongest context design?
options: Remove dates and section IDs
Put the task and hard constraints first, retrieve the regional exception with provenance, and place the decision question after focused evidence
Repeat all messages twice
Keep the entire case and policy corpus in one context, place the decision question at both ends, and rely on nominal capacity plus repetition for recall
questions.explanation: Focused retrieval and deliberate placement make critical evidence salient while preserving verifiability. Context capacity alone cannot guarantee that one buried rule controls the answer.

questions.objective: Calibrate confidence and human review
questions.prompt: Packet 1, HelioDesk: Which two cases should receive mandatory human review even if the ordinary automation path is accurate? Select two.
options: High-impact refund recommendations
Partial, conflicting, novel, or low-evidence cases
Outputs below a fixed self-reported confidence threshold calibrated on aggregate cases but not segmented by impact, novelty, or evidence state
Cases with unusually long input records
questions.explanation: Consequence and observable evidence risk should drive review. Self-reported percentages are not calibrated thresholds, and length does not reliably predict correctness or harm.

questions.objective: Track provenance, conflicts, dates, and content types
questions.prompt: Packet 1, HelioDesk: Two approved policy resources contain conflicting effective dates and no precedence rule. What should synthesis do?
options: Choose the longer document
Select the source with the newest visible effective date and record the other as supporting background, assuming recency defines precedence unless challenged
Preserve both source versions, block the governed action, and escalate the exact conflict to the policy owner
Average the dates
questions.explanation: An undefined conflict is a policy gap, not a model reasoning problem. Provenance must remain visible while the authorized owner resolves the governing source.

questions.objective: Choose coordinator and subagent topologies
questions.prompt: Packet 2, Ridgeway: A monorepo migration touches four independent service adapters plus one shared protocol. Which topology is strongest?
options: Run the cross-service review before inspecting adapters
Use one subagent for every deterministic test command
Give four adapter specialists the entire repository and shared write access, then ask a coordinator to resolve overlapping edits before running protocol tests
Build a manifest, run bounded adapter reviews in parallel, then perform one cross-service protocol pass after local results are validated
questions.explanation: Per-adapter work benefits from isolated parallel contexts, while the shared protocol requires a later global pass. A manifest enforces coverage and prevents duplicate ownership.

questions.objective: Enforce prerequisites, decompose concerns, and structure handoffs
questions.prompt: Packet 2, Ridgeway: Which two prerequisites should the orchestrator enforce structurally? Select two.
options: The coordinator should approve the consolidated design narrative before contract tests, because test failures can then be interpreted against intended behavior
All adapter specialists should update one shared manifest during execution so cross-service synthesis always sees the latest findings
Deterministic contract tests pass before a reviewer may recommend merge
Every in-scope adapter has a complete or named partial review before cross-service synthesis
questions.explanation: Coverage state and test gates have exact answers and belong in orchestration code. Style preference and shared unversioned notes cannot substitute for verified prerequisites.

questions.objective: Resume or fork without carrying stale context
questions.prompt: Packet 2, Ridgeway: During a long migration, the target dependency releases a breaking version and the branch changes. What should happen before continuing?
options: Reconcile files and dependency state against the manifest, mark stale assumptions, and start or fork with a revised plan if divergence is material
Resume from the compacted plan, re-run only the last failed command, and treat new branch or dependency differences as implementation details to absorb during edits
Resume and repeat the last writes
Delete all test evidence
questions.explanation: Conversation continuity is not authoritative external state. Reconciliation prevents duplicate writes and obsolete planning, while a fresh branch of reasoning protects the valid prior work.

questions.objective: Use hooks for deterministic controls and normalization
questions.prompt: Packet 2, Ridgeway: Which two hook uses are appropriate? Select two.
options: Run targeted formatting or contract tests after an edited file changes
Run a shell hook that compares the changed architecture to repository examples and blocks writes when its heuristic similarity score is too low
Block edits outside the declared migration scope before write
Record credential identifiers and resolved secret-store paths in hook output so failed CI operations can be reproduced without exposing raw values
questions.explanation: Scope gates and targeted verification are deterministic, observable hook responsibilities. Semantic design judgment belongs to reviewed reasoning, and secrets should never enter configuration or logs.

questions.objective: Choose Claude Code file, shell, and search tools safely
questions.prompt: Packet 2, Ridgeway: The agent knows the exact file and needs to change one existing function. Which tool sequence is strongest?
options: Use broad shell replacement across the repository
Read the known file, apply a bounded edit, then run the smallest relevant test command
Search for analogous functions across the repository, copy the most common implementation into the known file, and rely on the full test suite to expose local differences
Search the public web instead of the repository
questions.explanation: Specific file tools express intent and keep the diff inspectable. Shell remains appropriate for tests, but broad text mutation creates unnecessary scope and escaping risk.
